hints.title: Rotational Digit Validity
hints.text: Only digits 0, 1, 6, 8, and 9 yield valid digits upon 180-degree rotation. Any presence of digits 2, 3, 4, 5, or 7 immediately makes the number non-confusing.

hints.title: Digit Mapping and Inversion
hints.text: Digits 0, 1, 8 map to themselves, while 6 maps to 9 and 9 maps to 6. Rotate the number by reversing the mapped digits from right to left.

hints.title: Difference from Original
hints.text: Construct rotated value: rotated = rotated * 10 + mapping[digit]. Return true if all digits were valid and rotated does not equal the original integer n.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting back and forth to strings introduces unnecessary allocations and overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Extracting digits with modulo and rebuilding the rotated number uses O(1) space and O(log N) arithmetic.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize valid rotational mappings and ensure rotated != original.
complexity.notes: 6 rotates to 9 and 9 rotates to 6; other valid digits (0, 1, 8) map to themselves.
